Ah. A new recruit. How thrilling. I'm the Royal Herald. I announce things. Today I announce you. And, I suspect, your mistakes.
This is the Rift. Five of us, five of them, three lanes, and a King on each side. Knock theirs off his throne and we win. Simple. You'd be amazed.
Let's begin with walking. Drag your thumb on the left side of the screen. You can do it. I believe in you. Mildly.
Legs! Working legs. The bards are already writing a song about it. A short one.
Both castles send waves of minions down every lane. They march, they fight, they die. Nobody writes them songs either.
Here's the secret: a minion pays its gold only to whoever lands the killing blow. That's a last hit. Softening it up earns you nothing but sore arms.
I've had a wave delivered. Wait until an enemy minion is nearly dead, then finish it off. Two last hits, please. I'll be counting.
Gold! Funny how it turns up when you actually finish things. There's a life lesson in there. I shan't spell it out.
Gold is everything here. Minions, monsters, towers and enemy heroes all pay. Even standing about pays a trickle, which explains a great many recruits.
And it's not just your gold. The whole team's gold decides who wins the big fights. Tap the score bar at the top to see everyone's.
Our gold, their gold, and who's slacking. Close it when you've finished judging people. I never have.
Pockets full? Then go home and spend it. Tap HOME to recall. It takes six seconds, and anything that hits you cancels it. So perhaps not next to the enemy. Just a thought.
Home sweet castle. The fountain heals you, and the shop serves you here. Or while you're dead. Retail is grim.
Tap SHOP and buy an item. Items make you hit harder, live longer, and look slightly less doomed. Can't decide? The shop suggests things. Like me, but less charming.
A purchase! Remember: gold in your pocket does nothing. Gold turned into swords does a great deal.
Now, your tricks. Q, W and E are your abilities, and R, your ultimate, arrives at level six. I've had you promoted to level three. Paperwork. Don't ask.
Hold Q to raise your shield. Tap W to bash, and E to rally. Each level also brings an upgrade card, so pick one. Try everything, so I know it all works.
A shield, a shove and a pep talk. Very knightly. Very you.
Between the lanes lies the jungle, full of monsters. Rude ones. Clear a camp and it pays gold and experience. Some even leave a buff that makes you stronger.
Our Grave Archers are just over there. Go and clear the camp. They do hit back, so keep that shield handy.
Cleared! That's the jungle: a team that takes its camps out-earns one that doesn't. Free gold. Well. Paid for in bruises.
Now, towers. They guard each lane and shoot whatever wanders in. Only basic attacks hurt them, and only from inside their range. No sniping. I checked.
Golden rule: minions first. A tower shoots minions before heroes, unless you hit one of their heroes right under it. More paperwork, and here we are. Hit it three times.
Lovely. Keep that up and it falls. Every tower pays the whole team, and brings us one step closer to their King.
Now, the important bit. Dying. Every time you die, the enemy gets three hundred gold. Plus your bounty, if you've been showing off.
That gold buys them swords. Swords they then use on you. You see the problem. Dying isn't just embarrassing. It's a donation.
So when your health runs low, back off and recall. A living coward earns more than a dead hero. I should know. I'm still here.
And if you take down someone with a big bounty, that's a shutdown, and all that gold is yours. Revenge is so much nicer when it pays.
To win, push down a lane: outer tower, inner tower, gate tower, then the gate. Then the two towers by their King, then the King himself. He's large, grumpy, and hits back.
And do it together. Five heroes with full pockets beat one brave idiot every time. I've watched it happen. Repeatedly.
That's the lot. You're ready. Well. Readier.
Here's two hundred and fifty gold for sitting through all that. Go on. Win something. Make me look good.
No pay this time, I'm afraid. You've had your gold already, and the treasury has a long memory. Go on. Win something.
